questions.question:
**Directions: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. **

The forest officers ________ a leopard cub trapped in a pit.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 1), i.e., Discovered.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__** 

 
• The blank is used after the subject, indicating that the blank must contain the main verb of the sentence.
 
• Let's look at the **meaning **of the given words:-
 
• **Discovered **- find unexpectedly or during a search.
 
 
• For Example - Firemen **discovered **a body in the debris.
 
 
 
• **Founded **- establish or originate (an institution or organization).
 
 
• For Example - The monastery was **founded **in 1665.
 
 
 
• **Invented **- create or design (something that has not existed before); be the originator of.
 
 
• For Example - He **invented **an improved form of the steam engine.
 
 
 
• **Searched **- try to find something by looking or otherwise seeking carefully and thoroughly.
 
 
• For Example - I **searched **among the rocks, but there was nothing.
 
 
 
• We can eliminate **option 3 as the cub cannot be invented.**
 
• Found means to establish and search means to find something carefully but the sentence tries to convey the idea that they found a leopard cub **unexpectedly**.
 
• Thus, '**discovered**' is the most preferable option.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1.

 ​**

**Thus, the complete sentence is: ***The forest officers **discovered** a leopard cub trapped in a pit.*

questions.question:
**Directions:** **Fill in the blanks with the most appropriate words.**

They did it as you ________ them to.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2), i.e., Had told.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence uses the blank after the pronoun '**you**', indicating that it must contain a verb.
 
• The first verb of the sentence is the simple past tense '**did**'.
 
• Now, the sentence talks about them doing something as they were told by '**you**'.
 
• This suggests that the second action of 'telling them how to do' was done before 'they did it'.
 
• ** Important Point:**
 
• **Whenever an action has happened before another past event; the correct tense to be used is past perfect tense. *Example: I had gone home before my mother came back.***
 
• The second verb of the sentence, then, must be in past perfect tense form, which is, '**Had told**'__.

**Thus, the completed sentence is: ***They did it as you __**had told**__ them to.*

questions.question:
**Directions: Fill in the blanks with the most appropriate words.**

Rohit taught you such tricks as these, ________?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 1), i.e., Didn’t he.**

__
 
• **Explanation**:
 
• The sentence uses the blank after a statement and ends with a question mark, indicating that the blank must contain a question tag.
 
• The verb of the sentence is the positive simple past tense verb, '**taught**'.
 
• ** Important Point:**
 
• **Question Tag Rule 1: If the verb is positive, the question tag is always negative. *Example: You do know that, don't you?***
 
• ** Question Tag Rule 2: If the verb is in simple past tense, the question tag is 'Did/Didn't' + the appropriate pronoun for the subject. *Example: Ram said yes, didn't he? ***
 
• This means the correct question tag here would be '**Didn't he?**'__

**Thus, the completed sentence is: ***Rohit taught you such tricks as these, __**didn't he**__?*

questions.question:
Find out which part has an error and mark it as your answer. If there is no error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

She gave a (A)/ loud shout, which heard (B)/ across the village. (C)/ No error (D)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2), i.e. B**

__
 
• **Explanation**:
 
• The sentence uses the incorrect adjective phrase '**which heard**'.
 
• The second part of the sentence, 'heard across the village' is giving more information about the noun, 'a loud shout'.
 
• So, it is an adjective phrase, associated with the noun.
 
• ** Important Point:**
 
• Saying 'a loud shout, which heard' indicates that the shout itself heard something, which is incorrect.
 
• The grammatically correct form of the adjective phrase would be '**Which was heard**', suggesting it was heard across the village by people.__

**Thus, the rectified sentence is: ***She gave a loud shout, which **was heard** across the village.*

questions.question:
**Directions: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank**.

Will he be glad if you ________ my proposal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Accept__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The blank is used after the pronoun, indicating that it must contain a verb.
 
• Given the context of a proposal, the verb here should mean 'saying yes or no' to the proposal.__
 
• **Let's look at the meanings of the given options:**
 
• **Except**- not including; other than.
 
• **Expect**- regard (something) as likely to happen.
 
• **Intercept**- obstruct (someone or something) so as to prevent them from continuing to a destination.
 
• **Accept**- consent to receive or undertake (something offered).
 
• Out of these, only **Accept **can be an appropriate verb here.

**Thus, the completed sentence is: ***Will he be glad if you __**accept**__ my proposal?*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2cc014001a9a70d86735241cc35c82dd42b72fdf15c186a2bedcc9dce43fb549.png] 

__
 
• Pronoun के बाद रिक्त का उपयोग किया जाता है, यह दर्शाता है कि इसमें एक verb होनी चाहिए।
 
• एक प्रस्ताव के संदर्भ को देखते हुए, यहां verb का अर्थ प्रस्ताव के लिए 'हां या नहीं' कहना चाहिए।__
 
• आइए दिए गए विकल्पों के अर्थों को देखें:
 
• **Except** - शामिल नहीं; के अलावा अन्य।
 
• **Ex****pect** - संबंध (कुछ) होने की संभावना के रूप में।
 
• **Intercept** - किसी को (किसी चीज़ को) बाधित करना ताकि उन्हें एक गंतव्य के लिए जारी रखा जा सके।
 
• **Accept**- प्राप्त करने या शुरू करने के लिए सहमति (कुछ की पेशकश)।
 
• इनमें से केवल **Accept** ही यहां एक उपयुक्त **verb** हो सकती है।
